output.summary: A herbaceous perennial native across most of temperate Europe and western Asia, the cowslip is absent from some northern areas but reappears in northernmost Scotland and Scandinavia. It produces clusters of deep-yellow flowers in spring and frequently hybridizes with other primroses.
output.edibilityNote: Leaves were traditionally eaten as salad greens in Spain; historical English uses include flower-flavoured wine, sugared flowers, salads and boiled greens.
